messages.subject: Question regarding MStats output in spectronaut and error found after the
messages.subject_clean: Question regarding MStats output in spectronaut and error found after the
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a question regarding the use of MSstats for protein analysis of DIA data processed with Spectronaut.

I downloaded the TSV file named "_Report_MSstats Report (v3.7.3) (Normal)" from Spectronaut after disabling the cross-run normalization option in the Quantification settings. I then imported the file into R and converted it using:
msstats_input <- SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(...)

The resulting msstats_input.csv file contains the following columns:

colnames(msstats_input)
[1] "ProteinName" "PeptideSequence" "PrecursorCharge" "FragmentIon" [5] "ProductCharge" "IsotopeLabelType" "Condition" "BioReplicate" [9] "Run" "Fraction" "Intensity"

However, when I attempt to upload this file into MSstatsShiny, I receive the following error message:
>
> Failed to load data: The following columns are missing from the input data: FGCharge.

Should I select "MSstats Format" as the Type of File when importing the data instead? If so, is this option intended only for data generated from Spectronaut, or should the MSstats Format option be used for any dataset that has been converted with the MSstatsConvert package, regardless of the original software platform?

Thank you for your help.

Best regards,
Luisa Maria

messages.body_plain:
Hi Luisa,

We were not aware that Spectronaut has a new file TSV file named "_Report_MSstats Report".   In this case, you should select "MSstats Format".

This option was originally intended for any data that had been converted with the MSstatsConvert package regardless of the original software platform, but the option should also work in cases where the spectral processing tool does the conversion to MSstats format themselves (i.e. your specific case)

Thanks,
Tony

messages.subject: Question: How to treat DDA data of biotin labeled proteins, should we do a PTM or regular analysis?
messages.subject_clean: Question: How to treat DDA data of biotin labeled proteins, should we do a PTM or regular analysis?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
We have a dataset from an in vitro biotinylation assay, including samples processed both with and without an enrichment step. We analyzed the data using FragPipe and specified biotinylation as a variable modification.

While the analysis successfully identifies the modified sites, we were wondering whether, for the statistical analysis, it would be more appropriate to treat the dataset as a PTM dataset or as a protein/peptide dataset in the Biological Question section.

Additionally, if we use the MSstats Converter workflow, will the biotinylated modification be properly accounted for when using the FragPipetoMSstatsFormat() command?

Thank you for your help.

messages.subject: Re: Question: How to treat DDA data of biotin labeled proteins, should we do a PTM or regular analysis?
messages.subject_clean: Question: How to treat DDA data of biotin labeled proteins, should we do a PTM or regular analysis?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

It depends on your biological question. MSstatsPTM separates changes in biotinylated peptides from changes in overall protein abundance. If that adjustment matters for your question, use the PTM workflow. If not, the biotinylated peptides can be analyzed on their own with regular MSstats.

FragPipetoMSstatsFormat doesn't handle biotin specially. Biotinylated and unmodified forms of a peptide become separate features of the same protein, so a protein-level analysis averages the biotin signal in with everything else. To avoid that, keep only the rows whose PeptideSequence contains the biotin mass, for example [226.0776], before converting, or choose Peptide as the biological question in MSstatsShiny.

For the PTM route, use FragPipetoMSstatsPTMFormat from MSstatsPTM, with the enriched samples as input and the unenriched ones as input_protein. For label-free data, set

label_type = "LF", protein_id_col = "ProteinName", peptide_id_col = "PeptideSequence"

and set mod_id_col to the exact name of the biotin localization column in your data, for example "K:226.0776". MSstatsShiny's FragPipe PTM option only supports TMT, so label-free data needs this step in R.

Also, features measured in two runs or fewer are removed by default (removeFewMeasurements), so that's the likely reason if some biotinylated peptides go missing.

Best,
Swaraj
